summary: This note describes Southern California's Mediterranean climate and its geography, including the coastal and inland urban areas and population figures for its cities and metropolitan regions. It covers the 'Tech Coast' concept and the region's universities, professional and college sports teams, and major airports. It also notes the region's sprawling suburban development, its position as the third most populated megalopolis in the US, and its share of about 60 percent of California's population.
one_line: Overview of Southern California's climate, cities, metropolitan areas, universities, sports teams, and airports.
key_facts: Southern California has a Mediterranean climate with infrequent rain and many sunny days.
Los Angeles had a population of 3,792,621 and is the most populous city in California and the second most populous in the United States.
San Diego had a population of 1,307,402, making it the second most populous city in California and the eighth most populous in the nation.
The Greater Los Angeles Area had a population of 17,786,419, and the San Diego–Tijuana area had 5,105,768.
Southern California contains roughly 60 percent of California's population, with over 22 million people.
Southern California is the third most populated megalopolis in the United States, after the Great Lakes Megalopolis and the Northeastern megalopolis.
The Tech Coast moniker describes the region's diversified technology and industrial base and its research universities.
The region includes 5 University of California campuses (Irvine, Los Angeles, Riverside, Santa Barbara, and San Diego).
The region includes 12 California State University campuses, among them Bakersfield, Channel Islands, and San Luis Obispo.
The UCLA Bruins and the USC Trojans both field NCAA Division I teams in the Pac-12 Conference and have a longtime rivalry.
Los Angeles International Airport is the second-busiest airport in the United States by passenger volume.
San Diego International Airport is described as the busiest single runway airport in the world.
Van Nuys Airport is described as the world's busiest general aviation airport.
Camp Pendleton is the main gap to continued urbanization along Interstate 5 when traveling south.
Southern California's population encompasses seven metropolitan areas (MSAs), including the Los Angeles, Inland Empire, and San Diego metropolitan areas.
